content:
# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 4

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 24

---

## Disagreement 001 — v. 1: Framing of Simon's slander

- **EMET:** "slandered Onias as if he had been the one who incited Heliodorus"
- **LOGOS:** "slandered Onias as if it were he who had incited Heliodorus"
- **PNEUMA:** "spread the story that Onias himself had set up the whole Heliodorus affair"
- **Note:** PNEUMA paraphrases significantly. EMET and LOGOS are close. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 002 — v. 2: "no true high priest"

- **EMET:** "zealot for the laws"
- **LOGOS:** "zealot for the laws"
- **PNEUMA:** "devoted champion of the law"
- **Note:** All three render *zelōtēn tōn nomōn* consistently enough. PNEUMA uses "champion" rather than "zealot." SOPHIA uses "zealot."

## Disagreement 003 — v. 3: Simon's followers

- **EMET:** "murders were being committed by some of Simon's approved men"
- **LOGOS:** "murders were being carried out by some of Simon's associates"
- **PNEUMA:** "some of Simon's henchmen began committing murders"
- **Note:** "Approved men" (EMET) is overly literal. PNEUMA's "henchmen" adds a pejorative charge not explicit in Greek. LOGOS "associates" is neutral and appropriate. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 004 — v. 6: Simon's condition

- **EMET:** "impossible to obtain peace in affairs nor for Simon to cease from his folly"
- **LOGOS:** "impossible to achieve stability in public affairs or to put a stop to Simon's madness"
- **PNEUMA:** "no end to the turmoil, and Simon would never stop his madness"
- **Note:** "Folly" vs. "madness" for Greek *aphrosynē*. "Stability" vs. "peace" for affairs. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 005 — v. 7: Jason's acquisition

- **EMET:** "obtained the high priesthood by corrupt means"
- **LOGOS:** "obtained the high priesthood through corrupt means"
- **PNEUMA:** "bought his way into the high priesthood"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "bought his way" is vivid and accurate but idiomatic. EMET and LOGOS are formally equivalent. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 006 — v. 9: Athletic institution

- **EMET:** "a gymnasium and a body of youth for it"
- **LOGOS:** "a gymnasium and a corps of young men"
- **PNEUMA:** "a gymnasium and an athletic club for young men"
- **Note:** Greek *ephēbeion* — the corps of ephebes (young men in formal Hellenistic training). LOGOS's "corps" is most precise. SOPHIA uses "corps of young men."

## Disagreement 007 — v. 10: Immediate action

- **EMET:** "he at once shifted his compatriots over to the Greek way of life"
- **LOGOS:** "he immediately shifted his compatriots to the Greek way of life"
- **PNEUMA:** "immediately set about converting his fellow Jews to a Greek way of life"
- **Note:** PNEUMA substitutes "converting" for "shifted" — a stronger word with religious overtones. EMET/LOGOS use neutral "shifted." SOPHIA uses "shifted."

## Disagreement 008 — v. 12: Gymnasium location

- **EMET:** "right under the citadel"
- **LOGOS:** "right under the citadel itself"
- **PNEUMA:** "right under the shadow of the citadel"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "shadow" — not in Greek — for symbolic effect. LOGOS adds "itself" for emphasis. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 009 — v. 12: "wore the Greek hat"

- **EMET:** "wear the Greek hat"
- **LOGOS:** "wear the broad-brimmed Greek hat"
- **PNEUMA:** "wear the Greek broad-brimmed hat"
- **Note:** LOGOS and PNEUMA both add "broad-brimmed" for clarity. EMET is more literal. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 010 — v. 13: Jason's characterization

- **EMET:** "who was ungodly and no true high priest"
- **LOGOS:** "who was godless and no true high priest"
- **PNEUMA:** "The man was godless — no true high priest"
- **Note:** PNEUMA breaks into a separate sentence for rhetorical emphasis. LOGOS uses "godless" for *anosiōs*. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 011 — v. 14: The priests' abandonment

- **EMET:** "they hurried to take part in the unlawful proceedings in the wrestling arena after the call to the discus"
- **LOGOS:** "they hurried to take part in the unlawful activities in the wrestling arena at the first call of the discus"
- **PNEUMA:** "the moment the discus thrower called the athletes to the track, they were off to the wrestling grounds"
- **Note:** PNEUMA interprets "the call of the discus" as an athlete calling others, which may not be accurate. "The discus call" was likely a signal (a thrown discus summoning athletes). SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 012 — v. 15: "finest thing"

- **EMET:** "thinking the Greek forms of prestige to be the finest thing"
- **LOGOS:** "regarding the Greek forms of prestige as the finest thing of all"
- **PNEUMA:** "Greek prestige was all that mattered to them"
- **Note:** PNEUMA compresses and loses "forms of prestige." LOGOS adds "of all" for rhetorical force. SOPHIA uses "the highest good" for *ta kallista*.

## Disagreement 013 — v. 17: Authorial comment

- **EMET:** "For it is no light thing to act impiously against the divine laws — the time that follows will make this clear"
- **LOGOS:** "For it is no light thing to be impious toward the divine laws — and the time that follows will make this plain"
- **PNEUMA:** "To act with contempt toward the laws of God is no small matter. What came after made that devastatingly clear"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "devastatingly" and restructures into two sentences. LOGOS and EMET are very close. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 014 — v. 19: Jason's envoys

- **EMET:** "the vile Jason sent as spectators three hundred silver drachmas"
- **LOGOS:** "the vile Jason sent delegates as spectators, bearing three hundred drachmas"
- **PNEUMA:** "Jason sent envoys to attend as spectators — carrying three hundred silver drachmas"
- **Note:** LOGOS and PNEUMA both supply "delegates/envoys," clarifying that the spectators were sent persons. EMET's construction is ambiguous. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 015 — v. 22: Reception of Antiochus

- **EMET:** "ushered in with a blaze of torches and with shouts"
- **LOGOS:** "welcomed with torchlight processions and acclamations"
- **PNEUMA:** "torchlight processions, cheering crowds, a magnificent welcome"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "magnificent welcome" beyond the Greek. LOGOS's "acclamations" for shouts is appropriately formal. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 016 — v. 24: Menelaus's advantage

- **EMET:** "when he appeared to him as a man of dignified bearing and was advanced in wisdom"
- **LOGOS:** "and appeared before him as a man of considerable dignity"
- **PNEUMA:** "he sized up the opportunity and outbid Jason"
- **Note:** PNEUMA omits the character description of Menelaus entirely. EMET adds "advanced in wisdom" which is not in all manuscripts. SOPHIA follows LOGOS, dropping the questionable phrase.

## Disagreement 017 — v. 25: Menelaus's character

- **EMET:** "He had the temper of a cruel tyrant and the rage of a savage beast"
- **LOGOS:** "He had the disposition of a cruel tyrant and the rage of a savage beast"
- **PNEUMA:** "He had the heart of a tyrant and the temper of a wild beast"
- **Note:** "Disposition" vs. "temper" vs. "heart" for Greek *ēthos*. "Savage beast" vs. "wild beast." All convey the intended ferocity. SOPHIA follows EMET's phrasing.

## Disagreement 018 — v. 34: Onias's murder

- **EMET:** "using treachery and swearing oaths, he gave him his right hand in pledge"
- **LOGOS:** "extending false assurances and pledging with an oath while giving his right hand"
- **PNEUMA:** "extended a handshake, swore solemn oaths, and talked Onias into coming out"
- **Note:** The Greek specifies *dexian dous* (giving the right hand) — the most solemn pledge of good faith. PNEUMA's "handshake" is too casual. SOPHIA follows LOGOS with "pledging with an oath while extending his right hand."

## Disagreement 019 — v. 35: Universal condemnation

- **EMET:** "not only the Jews but many also of other nations were indignant and displeased"
- **LOGOS:** "not only the Jews but many from other nations as well were outraged and deeply aggrieved"
- **PNEUMA:** "Not just Jews — people from many other nations were furious and appalled"
- **Note:** PNEUMA's emphasis is more dramatic. "Furious and appalled" vs. "outraged and deeply aggrieved." SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 020 — v. 37: Antiochus's reaction

- **EMET:** "moved to pity, wept because of the sobriety and great propriety of the deceased"
- **LOGOS:** "moved to compassion; he wept because of the sober and restrained character of the deceased"
- **PNEUMA:** "He grieved, and he wept, thinking of the dignity and restraint that had marked the dead man's life"
- **Note:** "Sobriety" and "propriety" vs. "sober and restrained." Greek *sōphrosynē* and *kosmiotes*. SOPHIA uses "sobriety and uprightness."

## Disagreement 021 — v. 38: Andronicus stripped

- **EMET:** "stripped Andronicus of his purple and tore off his garments"
- **LOGOS:** "stripped Andronicus of his purple robe immediately, tore off his outer garments"
- **PNEUMA:** "had Andronicus stripped of his purple robe right there and then, tore the garments off him"
- **Note:** PNEUMA adds "right there and then" for dramatic immediacy. LOGOS adds "outer" for garments. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 022 — v. 40: Auranus description

- **EMET:** "a man advanced in years and no less advanced in folly"
- **LOGOS:** "a man as advanced in age as he was advanced in foolishness"
- **PNEUMA:** "as old as he was foolish"
- **Note:** Greek *prokekōphōs tē hēlikia kai tē anoia* — advanced in age and in stupidity. EMET and LOGOS preserve the parallelism. PNEUMA compresses. SOPHIA follows EMET.

## Disagreement 023 — v. 41: The improvised weapons

- **EMET:** "threw them all in a promiscuous confusion at Lysimachus and his men"
- **LOGOS:** "they hurled everything at Lysimachus and his men in wild confusion"
- **PNEUMA:** "They hurled everything at Lysimachus's men in a chaotic volley"
- **Note:** Greek *asymmiktos* — mixed/indiscriminate. "Promiscuous confusion" (EMET) is more literal; "wild confusion" (LOGOS) more natural. SOPHIA uses "wild confusion."

## Disagreement 024 — v. 47: "Scythians"

- **EMET:** "freed even if they had argued their case before Scythians"
- **LOGOS:** "freed without penalty had they pleaded before Scythians"
- **PNEUMA:** "walk free before the most barbarous court imaginable"
- **Note:** PNEUMA loses the specific Scythian reference. The Scythian allusion is a known proverb (Scythians as the barbarian standard). SOPHIA retains the Scythian reference per LOGOS.
